# MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 — Fastener inspection and torque - Machining shot blast cabinet #1

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Scope
- This maintenance manual covers inspection and torque verification for all accessible fasteners on Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01).  
- Activities in this document apply to mechanical and access fasteners that affect structural integrity, guarding, and component alignment.  
- Do not use this document for electrical terminations, pneumatic fittings, or for subsystems controlled by separate work instructions; see related documents SB-1010, SOP-P3-L3-04, and SOP-P3-L3-05 for interface requirements and permit processes.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on shot blast cabinets are exposed to vibration, abrasive media flow, and repeated access. Loose or overtorqued fasteners can cause misalignment, loss of containment, or premature wear of components.  
- Regular inspection and recorded torque verification reduce unplanned downtime and help detect progressive loosening or thread damage. Torque verification is a preventive measure to confirm that assembly clamping forces remain within acceptable condition for safe operation and correct alignments.  
- The cabinet interfaces with the building dust collection system. Note the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is 1590 Pa. This value is a process alarm threshold and must be recorded during any maintenance that opens media containment to ensure correct resealing and system integrity.

Tools
- Adjustable torque wrench suitable for fastener sizes used on EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Calibrate under the plant calibration program before use.  
- Hand tools as required for access panels and guards. Use non-marring tools where finish damage is a concern.  
- Inspection lamp and mirror for visual access to hidden fasteners.  
- Thread lubricant and anti-seize as specified in equipment BOM; the lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709. Apply only where threads show corrosion or where assembly documentation specifies lubrication for torque control.  
- Fastener identification tags and cable ties for temporary labeling of inspected items.  
- Records forms or electronic device for recording torque values, condition notes, and signatures.

Procedure
- Preparation and safety: Verify permissions and lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L3-04 and SOP-P3-L3-05. Confirm that media flow is stopped and that access is allowed. Consult SB-1010 for dust collection interface and confirm the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is not active before opening the cabinet. Wear required PPE for abrasive media and dust exposure.  
- Visual survey: Perform a walkthrough of the cabinet exterior and interior access points. Note any missing or damaged fasteners, signs of movement, or areas with abrasion. Mark locations requiring torque verification with temporary tags. This step documents baseline condition and identifies fasteners needing replacement rather than torque adjustment.  
- Fastener selection: Prioritize structural hold-downs, access panel retainers, hinge bolts, and guard fasteners. Where fasteners show corrosion or thread damage, replace rather than attempt to torque. Use fasteners and lubrication consistent with equipment parts lists and use CFW-LUB-709 only when lubrication is specified or when threads require treatment to achieve correct torque values.  
- Torque verification: Clean thread engagement surfaces and remove media deposits. Use the calibrated torque wrench to apply torque until the specified assembly feel is reached. If the assembly has no documented torque value in legacy records, confirm clamp condition visually and check for manufacturer torque data referenced in SB-1010 or equipment OEM files. Do not invent torque values; if values are not available, document condition and escalate to maintenance engineering. Record each torque verification entry on the maintenance record form with location, measured condition (tight, loose, or damaged), lubricant used if any, and operator initials.  
- Actions for nonconformance: If a fastener is loose, tighten to the documented value if available; if not available, replace the fastener and note the replacement on the record. If threads are damaged or stripped, install replacement hardware and update the parts list. If repeated loosening is observed at a location, add notes recommending lockwashers, threadlocker per engineering approval, or design review. For any activity that affects media containment, verify reseal before restarting operation and confirm dust collector alarm state as per SB-1010.  
- Post-maintenance verification: Close and secure all access panels. Perform a functional walk-around and, where practical, a short run-in verification per SOP-P3-L3-04 to confirm no abnormal vibration or noise. Verify that the dust collector pressure drop alarm for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) remains within normal indication and that no alarm is present.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners are verified as serviceable, properly torqued, or replaced and documented.  
- Records include location, condition notes, lubricant usage (CFW-LUB-709 if applied), and technician identification.  
- No evidence of progressive loosening remains at inspected interfaces; where repeated issues were found, engineering recommendations are recorded.  
- Dust collection alarm status is confirmed as normal following maintenance; the specific alarm threshold to reference is 1590 Pa for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01).  
- Any unresolved fastener condition that could affect safety or containment is escalated and a stop-work hold is placed until corrective actions are approved.

Examples and records to keep
- Example entry for maintenance log: location: access panel hinge, condition: light corrosion on threads, action: cleaned, CFW-LUB-709 applied, fastener torqued to documented value, technician: initials.  
- Example nonconformance entry: location: front guard lower bolt, condition: stripped thread, action: replaced fastener, note: recommend thread repair, technician: initials.  
- Required records: completed inspection checklist, torque verification sheet, replacement parts log, and any escalation paperwork. Retain all records per plant document retention policy and reference SB-1010 for storage location of dust collection interface records. Use SOP-P3-L3-05 for forms and sign-off workflow.

Related documents
- SB-1010  
- SOP-P3-L3-04  
- SOP-P3-L3-05
